sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Mag Mell was an Irish mythological site, also called Magh Meall. The terms plain of honey and plain of delights appear in several Irish narratives as descriptions of the Otherworld. There life is endlessly joyous and sweet. Trees bear blossoms and fruit at once. There is neither discomfort nor death. Although the name seems to imply a level place on land, Mag Mell is often described as a floating island. It is the domain of the sea god Manannán mac Lir.
objective: Document Mag Mell as an Irish Otherworld site and the domain of Manannán mac Lir.
